claim.quote: We present here experimental results on the production of antihydrogen in a pulsed mode in which the time when 90% of the atoms are produced is known with an uncertainty of ~250 ns.

key_value_text.quote: the time when 90% of the atoms are produced is known with an uncertainty of ~250 ns
key_value_text.value: Time at which 90% of the atoms are produced known to ~250 ns

name: Pulsed production of antihydrogen

significance.quote: the time when 90% of the atoms are produced is known with an uncertainty of ~250 ns
significance.value: Production time of 90% of the atoms known to an uncertainty of about 250 ns

summary.plain: AEgIS made antihydrogen in short pulses, so that the moment when 90 per cent of the atoms are produced is known to about 250 nanoseconds. The paper calls this a major landmark towards a direct gravity test on antimatter.
summary.technical: Charge exchange between laser-excited Rydberg positronium (from a pulsed positron beam on a nanochanneled Si target) and trapped, cooled antiprotons gives pulsed antihydrogen with a production time known to ~250 ns for 90% of the atoms.

title: Pulsed production of antihydrogen
why_it_matters: The abstract calls pulsed production a major landmark in the AEgIS experiment to perform direct measurements of the validity of the Weak Equivalence Principle for antimatter.
